title: Homo Fluxus v2.0 — A Civilization Map Through Energy-Flow Cosmology: From Grid to Governance — One Gradient, All Regimes
description: Systems-level map extending Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) across biology, cognition, economy, governance, and AI, defining Homo Fluxus as a dynamic entropy-gradient process rather than a static entity. v2.0 anchors the framework empirically: in human connectomes, local structure (degree ratio) predicts the functional variability gradient (κ) with r ≈ −0.97, while a global graph metric (Fiedler eigenvalue λ₂) fails (r ≈ 0.16), supporting the EFC principle that local structure governs energy/information flow.

efc_chain.description: The EFC causal chain: substrate (Grid) shapes energy flow (EF), which forms structure (S), driving dynamics (D), culminating in cognition (C).

hf_definition.description: Operational definition of Homo Fluxus as cognition aware of and aligned with its underlying energy-flow through structure and dynamics.

local_structure_anchor.description: Empirical anchor: the functional variability gradient \kappa is strongly (negatively) correlated with a local structural metric (degree ratio) at the individual subject level.

global_metric_failure.description: Global graph connectivity (Fiedler eigenvalue \lambda_2) shows negligible predictive power for \kappa, indicating locality of governing structure.

key_results.main_finding: Local structure (degree ratio) predicts the brain’s functional variability gradient (κ) with r ≈ −0.97, while a global metric (λ₂) is not predictive (r ≈ 0.16), supporting the EFC principle that local structure governs flow.
datasets_used: Human structural connectomes and functional variability gradients (DOI: 10.6084/m9.figshare.31940370)

sealed_predictions.statement: In independent human connectome datasets, local structural metrics (e.g., degree ratio or closely related local measures) will robustly outperform global graph metrics (e.g., λ₂) in predicting the functional variability gradient κ, with strong negative correlations (|r| > 0.8).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Compute correlations between κ and both local and global structural metrics across new cohorts; if global metrics match or exceed local metrics, P1 is falsified.

sealed_predictions.statement: Targeted alterations to local structural connectivity that modify degree ratio will produce directionally consistent shifts in regional functional variability κ.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Pre/post intervention studies (e.g., lesion models, stimulation-modulated connectivity, or longitudinal plasticity) measuring structural degree ratio and κ; absence of predicted shifts falsifies P2.

kill_criteria: KC1: Across independent connectome datasets, local structural metrics (e.g., degree ratio) fail to predict κ (|r| < 0.3) and are consistently outperformed by global metrics such as λ₂.

KC2: Direct physiological measurements demonstrate sustained cognitive function without net entropy export or neg-entropic maintenance at the organismal level, contradicting EFC’s requirement that cognition is a neg-entropic process.

KC3: Thermodynamic flow models cannot reproduce galaxy rotation curves without dark matter and are decisively disfavored versus ΛCDM (e.g., overwhelming model-comparison evidence), undermining the cross-regime EFC principle.
KC4: Empirical studies show reward shaping in RLHF does not track entropy minimization across architectures and tasks, breaking the proposed RLHF–thermodynamics isomorphism.
abstract: Homo Fluxus defines the human as a dynamic gradient system embedded in the same entropy-flow dynamics that govern the cosmos. The EFC chain Grid->EF->S->D->C is applied across biology, cognition, economy, energy, governance, and AI. v2.0 adds empirical anchor: degree ratio determines functional variability in the human brain (r~-0.97).
